Prepare a conservation feature for multiscale planning

load_multiscale_feature.Rd

Extracts feature amounts from raster or vector data and prepares them for use across a nested H3 planning-unit hierarchy. The returned planning-unit object contains a native-resolution feature column for reporting and a multiscale feature column used to represent the feature across resolutions.

Usage

load_multiscale_feature(
  pu,
  source,
  native_res,
  maps,
  feature_name = NULL,
  res_col = "res",
  opt_prefix = "msopt_",
  overwrite = FALSE,
  scale_raster_by_area = TRUE,
  value_col = NULL
)

Arguments

pu

An sf planning-unit object. Its row order must match maps.

source

A single-layer SpatRaster, RasterLayer, RasterStack, RasterBrick, sf, or sfc object containing the feature data.

native_res

Integer H3 resolution at which the feature is represented for reporting.

maps

A hierarchy object returned by build_h3_maps().

feature_name

Optional feature name. When NULL, a name is inferred from source.

res_col

Character name of the planning-unit resolution column.

opt_prefix

Character prefix used for the multiscale feature column.

overwrite

Logical; should existing output columns be replaced?

scale_raster_by_area

Logical; should raster means be multiplied by planning-unit area?

value_col

Optional character name of a value column in a vector source. When NULL, vector amounts are based on geometry measure alone.

Value

The input pu object with a native-resolution feature column, a multiscale feature column, and metadata describing the feature.

Details

Feature amounts are extracted from planning units at native_res or finer. Coarser planning units receive amounts aggregated through the H3 hierarchy. The native-resolution column contains the feature amount at native_res, while the multiscale column records the amounts used to represent the feature across resolutions. By default, these columns are named r<resolution>_<feature> and msopt_<feature>.

Where finer planning units completely partition a parent, the parent amount is obtained by summing child amounts. Where finer planning units cover only part of a parent, the feature amount in the uncovered parent area is combined with the child amounts.

For raster data, values are extracted with exactextractr::exact_extract() using a mean weighted by raster-cell coverage fraction. By default, this mean is multiplied by the extracted geometry area in square kilometres to produce an area-scaled feature amount. With scale_raster_by_area = FALSE, the coverage-weighted mean is used directly.

Polygon features contribute area in square kilometres, line features contribute length in kilometres, and point features contribute counts. Single and multipart geometries can be combined within one geometry family; each point in a MULTIPOINT is counted separately. Sources mixing polygons, lines, or points, and GEOMETRYCOLLECTION features, must be separated before loading. Supplying value_col weights these amounts by the corresponding source values.

See also

Other multiscale minimum-set: add_multiscale_min_set(), add_multiscale_min_set_objective(), add_multiscale_relative_targets(), build_multiscale_atoms(), build_multiscale_feature_atoms(), build_multiscale_objective_data(), eval_multiscale_atom_solution(), multiscale_feature_cols()

Examples

# Create one H3 parent and one of its children.
parent <- "872a1072bffffff" 
child <- h3jsr::get_children(parent, 8L, simple = TRUE)
child <- as.character(unlist(child, use.names = FALSE))[1]

h3_vec <- c(parent, child)

pu <- h3jsr::cell_to_polygon(h3_vec, simple = FALSE)
pu <- pu[match(h3_vec, pu$h3_address), ]
pu$res <- c(7L, 8L)

maps <- build_h3_maps(pu,res_levels = c(7L, 8L))

# Feature occupies the child planning unit.
feature <- sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_geometry(pu[2, ]))

pu <- load_multiscale_feature(pu = pu,source = feature,
  native_res = 8L,maps = maps,feature_name = "habitat")

sf::st_drop_geometry(pu)[,c("h3_address", "res", "r8_habitat", "msopt_habitat")]
#>        h3_address res r8_habitat msopt_habitat
#> 1 872a1072bffffff   7    0.00000       0.74037
#> 2 882a1072b1fffff   8    0.74037       0.74037
multiscale_feature_cols(pu)
#>      r8_habitat 
#> "msopt_habitat"
